hero.heading: What this component does
hero.description: A thin line used to visually separate content into distinct sections or groups, such as list rows, cards, or menu items. Orientation sets whether the line runs horizontal or vertical. It's a static, non-interactive element with no content of its own, choose the orientation that matches the layout direction it needs to divide.

rows.Description: Use to separate stacked content in a vertical layout, like rows in a list or sections on a page.
Use to separate side-by-side content, like items in a horizontal row or a toolbar.

rows.What changes: Divider has no interactive states. Orientation is fixed at placement and never changes at runtime.

rows.Description: None. Divider is a static visual element, it does not animate or transition between states or orientations.
Divider has no content slots. It renders only the separator line and holds no text, icon, or nested elements.

sections.title: Anatomy
rawTextContent: The only visible part. Renders as a horizontal or vertical stroke depending on Orientation, 1px thick (stroke/thin token)
Resizes via constraints to fill the width (horizontal) or height (vertical) of its container. The default 320×1 / 1×40 size is a starting size, not a fixed limit
0px on all corners (radius/none token), the same for both orientations

sections.title: How to use
dos: Choose Orientation to match the layout direction, horizontal to separate stacked content, vertical to separate side-by-side content.
Resize the instance to fill its container rather than leaving it at the default 320×1 (or 1×40) size, the line stretches with the frame.
donts: Don't use Divider as a spacing or margin mechanism, it's a visual line with no built-in padding, use layout gap for spacing between elements instead.

sections.title: Accessibility & Content Guidelines
items: Non-interactive and not focusable, Divider carries no keyboard or focus behavior of its own
In code, expose it with the platform's separator role (and an orientation attribute for the vertical variant) so assistive technology announces it correctly
Uses the border/default semantic token for its color, which resolves separately for light and dark mode, don't override it with a hardcoded color

rows.Description: 1px, bound to the stroke/thin token, the same for both orientations.
Not fixed. Constraints on the internal line stretch it to fill the available width (horizontal) or height (vertical) when the instance is resized.
0px, bound to the radius/none token, hard edges on both orientations.
border/default token. Resolves to a light neutral gray in light mode and a darker neutral gray in dark mode, so it stays visible in both themes automatically.
